overall_diagnosis: The pipeline for video-silence-remover depends on a normalized (sorted, clamped, non-overlapping) removal-interval list, but the segment-combiner documentation currently describes only naive concatenation/sorting. This mismatch causes downstream ffmpeg processing and duration/report accounting to be unreliable when detectors output overlapping or adjacent segments. video-processor/SKILL.md references de-overlap/clamp in the pipeline, but does not fully align its call expectations and completion checks with a clearly specified combined-segments contract.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The documented behavior is “combine and sort” only, with no required interval normalization. In silence/pause workflows, detector outputs frequently overlap or touch; without merging/de-overlap, the combined list can contain duplicated/invalid removals, inconsistent durations, and can break downstream ffmpeg processing or produce incorrect removed-duration totals.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Update the skill contract to require normalization after reading all inputs: (1) validate each segment has numeric start/end, (2) clamp to a non-negative timeline and (when duration is known/provided) clamp end<=total_duration, (3) drop/repair segments where end<=start, (4) sort by start then merge overlapping or directly-adjacent intervals (document rule: merge when next.start <= prev.end; optionally define adjacency tolerance if needed), (5) recompute duration=end-start for every output segment and recompute totals from merged segments, (6) document output guarantees: sorted, non-overlapping, within bounds, duration-consistent; include an example showing two overlapping/touching segments merged into one and note compatibility with video-processor/report-generator.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The pipeline/completion guidance depends on “combined, clamped, de-overlapped” segments, but the documented expectations are not tightly aligned to a concrete combined-segments format/guarantee. This can lead to calling process_video.py with unsafe intervals and failing completion checks or producing inconsistent compression metrics.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Revise the workflow section and completion gate to explicitly require using a normalized merged removal-segments JSON (as defined by the repaired segment-combiner) before invoking video processing. Add explicit pre-ffmpeg checks: intervals sorted, non-overlapping, 0<=start<end<=video_duration, and duration fields match end-start. Document the exact JSON shape expected/accepted for removal segments and how to pass it to process_video.py. Ensure the completion checks clearly reference the required output artifacts (/root/compressed_video.mp4 and /root/compression_report.json) and that any referenced paths/filenames in the instructions are consistent.
